title: The Requisition — Aftermath
description: The Requisition held everything and refused nothing, because it had no stamp for refused. The party's draw empties its column, and a held thing with no line to be held against is only a thing on a street. It turns the crates round itself, unasked, and enters the one word it never had a stamp for. Still the ledger's voice, never 'I'.

steps.text: The ledger frame had gone over in the fight, and its pages lay fanned across the cobbles, every column still adding. The Requisition stood among the stacks with its pen raised over a line it had not yet headed.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: ENTRY: one unauthorised draw. Amount: the column.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: The column does not balance. The column has never not balanced.

lines.speaker: Rogue
lines.text: So write 'robbed'. You've got a stencil for everything else.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: There is no stamp for refused. There is no stamp for lost. The stamps were cut before either was needed.

lines.speaker: Cleric
lines.text: What happens to all these crates now?

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: HELD. Held pending funding. Funding is... drawn. The line they were held against is closed.

lines.speaker: Mage
lines.text: Then nothing's holding them. They're just crates.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: A held thing with no line is not held. It is a thing on a street.

lines.speaker: Bard
lines.text: A whole street of things on a street. Somebody write a song.

lines.speaker: Fighter
lines.text: Or just turn them round. Approved side out.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: Orientation is not recorded. Which way round a thing was set down was never a line.

steps.text: It went to the nearest crate, set its hand flat on the stencil, and turned it so that APPROVED faced the street. Then the next one, and the one after that. Nobody had asked it to. There was no line for it.

lines.speaker: The Requisition
lines.text: ENTRY: crates, the top street, all of them. Disposition...

steps.text: Down the top street, a shopkeeper who had waited a very long time for a crate of nails began, carefully, to look hopeful.
